text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- INCOME DISTRIBUTION IS WORSE THAN IN 1992
Income distribution has improved after the Real stabilization plan but not enough to prevent Brazil from showing in 1996 one of the worst distribution levels since the 1980s.
-- BANK LIQUIDATIONS KICK OFF BROAD INVESTIGATION INTO FRAUD SCHEME

Brazilian financial markets will open Monday with an eye on investigations into a multi-million fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds. Observers believe the liquidation of 15 financial institutions was just the first stage of a broad investigation into the fixed income market.
-- EIGHT LANDLESS WORKERS HURT IN CONFLICT AT PONTAL
Eight landless workers were shot by security guards at Sao Domingos farm at Pontal do Paranapanema in Sao Paulo state after a group of 2,500 landless workers invaded the property.
-- BRAZIL LOSES REVENUES WITH U.S. BARRIERS
Agricultural producers estimate that Brazilian exports of primary goods to the United States would rise by at least $2 billion a year without U.S. barriers.
-- CONGRESS TO INVESTIGATE DEBENTURES ISSUED BY STATE FIRMS
A Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) investigating a multi-million fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds will look into debenture issues by state power firms Cesp and Eletrobras.
-- FRAUD SCHEME TO BE INVESTIGATED IN PARAGUAY

Brazil's Central Bank will ask the central bank of Paraguay to break the bank secrecy of brokerages, foreign exchange houses and firms involved in a multi-million fraud scheme involving municipal and state bonds.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
